title: First Territorial Division of the Earth
summary: CFAH's first stage of the division of the earth among Noah's descendants (Gen 10:5, 25, 32), dated 2254/2253 B.C.
description: CFAH-4 treats the territorial division as a seven-year process beginning 2254 B.C. and finalized 2247 B.C. (AP-27, AP-28). Derived from Berossus's 34,080 days from the Flood to the first dynasty of Babylon plus Cush's 62-year reign, counted back from the Dispersion.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 4: Dating Creation and the Deluge," ARJ 16 (2023): 475–489, section "AP-27: First Territorial Division: 2254/2253 B.C."

chronologies.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

chronologies.date: "in his [Peleg's] days was the earth divided"; "by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood"
chronologies.note: Scripture gives no year for the division beyond Peleg's lifetime.
Ussher has no separate first division; he links the division to Peleg's birth (1757 AM, 2247 BC) conditionally. See final-territorial-division.

Jordan does not distinguish a first territorial division; he treats the division of Gen 10:25 as the Babel scattering, which he places arbitrarily in AM 1871 (see final-territorial-division / dispersion). Not stated in the Jordan sources read (Biblical Horizons "Biblical Chronology" category, all 9 pages; garynorth.com archive of Biblical Chronology 1989-1996). Left empty, not inferred.
